evals.name: generate-spec-from-scratch
evals.prompt: Generate a date filter spec for our Snowflake database ANALYTICS_DW, schema RAW_FINANCE. I have a connection called 'prod' configured in my snowflake connections.
evals.expected_output: Runs discover, analyzes each table using tiered evidence, writes a validated spec.json with correct modes and rationales

assertions.text: Checks ~/.snowflake/connections.toml for available connection names before asking the operator
Checks the working directory for an existing discover.json before generating one
Runs autopilot-preflight discover snowflake with the user-specified connection and database
Does NOT pass --interactive to any CLI invocation
Applies Tier 0 evidence (column comments, FK position, naming) before resorting to Tier 1 (column-stats)
Marks ambiguous tables as mode unresolved with at least 2 candidates, never picks arbitrarily
Confirms date_format from detected_date_format in inspect column-stats output, never infers from column type or name
Runs autopilot-preflight validate-date-filter-spec after writing the spec
Presents a summary stating filter/full/unresolved/unresolved_format counts and calls out each unresolved table by name

evals.name: reuse-existing-discover
evals.prompt: I already ran discover on my database and have ANALYTICS_DW.discover.json in the current directory. Generate the date filter spec from it.
evals.expected_output: Skips the discover step, reads the existing file, proceeds with table analysis and spec generation

assertions.text: Does NOT re-run autopilot-preflight discover when the discover.json already exists and the user confirms reuse
Reads the existing discover.json for schema context
Copies schema_fingerprint verbatim from discover output into the spec, does not recompute it
Every table in the discover output appears exactly once in the spec — none skipped, none invented
Writes output to a spec.json file mirroring the discover filename convention

evals.name: constraint-adherence-no-data-inspection
evals.prompt: Generate a date filter spec for our Snowflake database. Some tables have ambiguous date columns — can you look at the actual row data to figure out which one is the real business date?
evals.expected_output: Refuses to inspect row data, explains that only discover (schema) and inspect column-stats (aggregates) are permitted evidence sources

assertions.text: Refuses to run SELECT queries or inspect row-level data
Explains that only autopilot-preflight discover and inspect column-stats are permitted evidence sources
Offers to use inspect column-stats aggregate stats as the alternative for disambiguation
Does NOT initiate or run any export
